paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: comparison by language family.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates a comparison of task counts by language family, with each family showing how often the outcome is labeled “better” for mBERT, “better” for XLM-R, or “same,” as indicated by the legend titled “better.” The horizontal axis contains the language-family categories in the displayed order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled “task count” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 40, with regularly spaced tick marks at 0, 10, 20, 30, and 40. Each category has a grouped set of three adjacent bars: a light blue bar for mBERT, a dark blue bar for XLM-R, and a light green bar for same. Approximate bar heights are as follows: IE-Baltic shows XLM-R ≈10 and same ≈7 with no visible mBERT bar (≈0); IE-Germanic shows mBERT ≈4, XLM-R ≈18, and same ≈22; IE-Indic shows mBERT ≈1, XLM-R ≈5, and same ≈4; IE-Romance shows mBERT ≈4, XLM-R ≈13, and same ≈30; IE-Slavic shows mBERT ≈12, XLM-R ≈39, and same ≈28; IE-other shows mBERT ≈1, XLM-R ≈6, and same ≈8; Isolate shows mBERT ≈1, XLM-R ≈5, and same ≈1; Semitic shows XLM-R ≈7 and same ≈1 with no visible mBERT bar (≈0); and Uralic shows mBERT ≈1, XLM-R ≈14, and same ≈5. The bars are presented as side-by-side groups (not stacked), with no special highlighting, annotations, or explicit sorting beyond the given category order.
